relevance.silbernagel-2007-pain-monitoring: This is the classic primary source for the app's clean/hold/back-off rule: keep loading while pain stays within set limits and returns to baseline by the next morning. Caveat: the evidence comes from Achilles tendon, not a knee ligament. The app's own 0-10 cut-offs are adapted from this model rather than tested in knees.
relevance.smith-2017-painful-exercise: Supports the app accepting low pain during a set (3/10 or under, not climbing) as 'clean' rather than demanding zero pain. Caveat: the trials studied chronic pain conditions, not an acute or subacute ligament injury.
relevance.sprague-2021-pain-guided: Carries the pain-monitoring model to a knee-region tissue (the patellar tendon) under heavy lifting. This is the closest knee application found. It is a feasibility pilot, not proof that the model works.
relevance.thomee-1997-pfps-pain-monitoring: Early knee source for the pain-monitoring system that Silbernagel later tested. It is cited for where the app's rule comes from, not as evidence that it works.
relevance.grindem-2016-delaware-oslo: A classic primary source for 90% strength-symmetry return-to-sport rules, the lineage of the app's within-10% single-leg strength gates. Caveats: isokinetic quadriceps testing, not leg press, and an ACLR population.
relevance.losciale-2019-rts-criteria: An honest counterweight to Grindem 2016 for the Gate 3 strength item: passing symmetry gates lowers risk only uncertainly. It supports keeping the ortho/PT sign-off and the other gate items.
relevance.zhou-2024-rts-reinjury: The most recent pooled estimate found for criteria-based clearance. It gives modest support for testing before return, in a surgical population.
relevance.piussi-2024-time-to-rts: Supports the app's stance that time alone is a weak guide and that rushing carries some risk, so phase dates are estimates and the gates decide.
relevance.van-melick-2016-acl-practice-guideline: This is the closest guideline template for the app's four phases with test-based gates between them. It was written for reconstructed knees, so the app adapts the structure rather than the surgical timelines.
relevance.ardern-2016-bern-consensus: Supports Gate 3's shared-decision items (clinician sign-off and the athlete's own trust) and Phase 4's graded return to lacrosse rather than a single pass/fail day.
relevance.svantesson-2024-mcl-nonoperative: The closest population found to Shawn's (non-operative knee ligament sprain), so useful context for the strength-first Phase 1-2 approach. It cannot tell us which exercises or doses work. Phase researchers may also cite it.
relevance.eitzen-2010-progressive-5-week: Supports Phase 1's premise that an injured, non-operated knee tolerates a progressive loading block early. This is the non-operative pathway, though for ACL rupture, not a sprain.
relevance.filbay-2025-rehab-alone-vs-aclr: Shows that a non-operative route back to sport is realistic for some knee ligament injuries. The population and the certainty both limit how far this applies to Shawn.
relevance.murray-2024-mlki-consensus: Explains why a non-operative multi-ligament sprain sits outside most of the literature, and why Gate 3 requires an ortho or PT sign-off before contact. The rehab content of the consensus is not in the abstract.
relevance.diermeier-2020-panther-acl-treatment: Lacrosse is a cutting and pivoting sport. This is the rationale for a specialist sign-off before contact and for treating any giving-way episode as a red flag, not a hold.
relevance.sturgill-2009-effusion-stroke-test: Backs the idea that swelling can be tracked and used to steer progression, which is the basis of the no-swelling gates and the next-morning check. The app relies on self-observation, which this study did not test.
relevance.palmieri-smith-2013-pain-effusion-quadri: Mechanism for why swelling counts as a back-off signal: it switches off the quadriceps that the program is trying to build. Caveat: a later study (Johnson 2024, PMID 39480795) found little effect of natural effusion size after ACL injury.
relevance.kikuchi-2024-effusion-3-months: Suggests that lingering swelling around three months goes with later strength deficits, which supports making 'no swelling' a gate item. This is an association, not cause, and it comes from a surgical population.
relevance.huang-2026-effusion-activity: Links how much load the knee takes to how much it swells. That is the logic behind checking for swelling after runs, lifts and plyos before progressing. Association only.
relevance.rambaud-2018-return-to-running: Context for an early-phase symmetry gate looser than the later 90% gates (Gate 1's within 20%). It describes common practice; it does not validate 80% or 70% as safe.
relevance.sayer-2024-running-criteria-survey: Shows that the app's run gate (no next-morning swelling or pain flare) matches common clinical practice, including for non-operative knees. This is practice consensus, not outcome evidence.
relevance.coleman-2024-deload-rct: Shows that a deload costs little but is not free. The app's deload keeps the same loads and cuts sets by a third, which is milder than the full break tested here. There is no injury-rehab data.
relevance.pancar-2026-deload-within-subject: Closest match to the app's schedule (reduced-volume weeks every fourth week). It suggests the planned deloads give up little. It was a healthy population with single-joint machine exercises.
relevance.bell-2023-deload-delphi: Gives the working definition behind the app's deload weeks. It is coaching consensus, not trial evidence.
relevance.buckthorpe-2019-late-stage-rehab: Rationale for Phase 3 (power, deceleration, plyometrics) and Phase 4 (sport-specific build-up). It is opinion-level evidence.
relevance.faltstrom-2026-on-field-rehab: The closest available template for Phase 4's rungs, which climb from straight-line running toward lacrosse with a clean-twice rule per rung. Lacrosse itself is not represented in it.
relevance.della-villa-2026-on-field-rehab-cohort: Supports spending real time in a graded on-field phase (Phase 4) before full lacrosse. This is an association in a surgical population.
relevance.pamboris-2024-okc-ckc: Supports keeping the leg extension (quad pattern) alongside leg press and squats. Caveat: ACL populations, and the strength findings rest on single trials. GRADE certainty read from the review's Table 8/9 in the open-access full text.
relevance.perriman-2018-okc-ckc: Balances Pamboris 2024. Together they suggest open and closed chain quad work are both acceptable, with no signal of laxity harm. The population is post-ACLR, not a non-operative multi-ligament sprain.
relevance.escamilla-1998-okc-ckc-biomechanics: A classic primary source behind the common practice of choosing exercise and range by which ligament is healing. Useful context for the squat and quad patterns, but it is modeled data from healthy men.
relevance.escamilla-2001-squat-biomechanics: Fits the program's progression from box squats to a bench and the leg press toward deeper ranges. Expert-level evidence only.
relevance.kassiano-2025-unilateral-bilateral: Explains why Phase 2 shifts to split squats and the single-leg press when the gates test single-leg strength. The evidence comes from healthy trainees.
relevance.graham-2026-rfess-acl: Caveat for g2-bulgarian: equal loads side to side do not prove the injured knee is doing equal work. It supports filming or watching form alongside the load comparison.
relevance.wellsandt-2017-lsi-overestimate: Explains a limit of every within-X% leg press gate: if the good leg is detrained too, symmetry overstates recovery. It argues for watching absolute single-leg loads climb, not just the ratio.
relevance.nagai-2020-hop-vs-strength-lsi: Supports using a single-leg leg press strength comparison as a gate separate from the hop tests. Caveat: the leg press here measured power in a bilateral press, not a single-leg rep max.
relevance.clark-2019-sl-leg-press-reliability: The closest evidence that a machine single-leg leg press is a trustworthy side-to-side test. The app's gate uses an 8-rep max, and test-to-test noise means a borderline 10% gap should be repeated.
relevance.girdwood-2025-quad-hamstring-strength-ac: Supports prioritizing quad and hamstring work throughout, and treating a passed symmetry gate as a minimum. The population had surgery, and strength loss after a non-operative sprain may differ.
relevance.kyritsis-2016-discharge-criteria: Supports training hamstrings as hard as quads (leg curls, Nordics, RDLs) and having a strength gate before contact. Caveat: isokinetic testing in surgical patients.
relevance.girdwood-2024-hip-calf-strength-acl: Puts the hip and calf patterns in proportion: worth training and testing (the g2-calf-raises gate), but the knee-spanning thigh muscles are where deficits usually sit.
relevance.nascimento-2018-hip-knee-pfp: The strongest synthesis found for hip work improving knee symptoms, but it covers kneecap pain, not ligament injury. It supports the hip pattern as an adjunct, not a substitute for quad work.
relevance.xiao-2025-proximal-core-acl: Supports hip-pattern exercises (abduction, hip thrusts, band walks) as part of movement-control work. The surrogate outcomes are biomechanical, not reinjury.
relevance.cashman-2026-hip-strength-valgus: A caution against assuming that hip machines alone will fix knee drift on the step-down gate. Practice and control of the movement itself likely matter too.
relevance.haroy-2019-adductor-programme: The rationale for the Copenhagen plank in the hip pattern for a field-sport return. It addresses groin protection, not the knee itself. A 2026 Copenhagen meta-analysis surfaced in the search was retracted and is excluded.
relevance.van-dyk-2019-nordic-hamstring: The rationale for Nordic negatives in the hamstring pattern as a lacrosse-return safeguard. Show it alongside impellizzeri-2021-nordic-reappraisal so the disagreement is visible.
relevance.impellizzeri-2021-nordic-reappraisal: The counterweight to van Dyk 2019; both belong on the hamstring pattern. Its moderate grade reflects the RCT-only design under our rule, not confidence that Nordics work: its finding is that the benefit is unproven.
relevance.crawford-2025-rdl-vs-nordic: Supports the hinge pattern (DB/Smith/single-leg RDL) as a valid hamstring stimulus and as an alternative when Nordics are not tolerated. Outcomes are architectural, not injury.
relevance.visser-2025-heel-rise-norms: Shows that the gate's 20 single-leg raises per side sits a little below typical healthy performance, and that legs should match. Per decision 8, these norms are text only and must not become a chart band.
relevance.hebert-losier-2017-heel-rise-reliability: Supports a rep-count calf gate as a stable, repeatable test. Their protocol used a 10-degree incline to fatigue, which differs from a step-edge calf raise, so counts are not directly comparable.
relevance.silva-2019-lateral-step-down-review: The main rationale for the g2-step-down gate. Its link to stiff ankles also suggests checking ankle mobility when the knee drifts inward.
relevance.werner-2019-fppa-reliability: Backs the gate's 'on video' wording: a phone video of the step-down is a reasonably repeatable check. The knee and hip had the largest detectable-change values, so small day-to-day differences in knee angle can still be noise.
relevance.gomes-2023-single-leg-squat-visual: Honest caveat for the g2-step-down gate: 'no inward knee drift' judged by eye is a coarse screen, not a validated pass/fail. It fits the gate's met-twice rule.
relevance.al-attar-2022-plyometric-acl-prevention: Supports keeping plyometrics in Phase 3 and in the lacrosse-phase warm-up. It is one of the few syntheses with a male subgroup (Shawn is male), but the male estimate is imprecise. This is prevention in healthy athletes, not rehab.
relevance.webster-2018-acl-prevention-meta: Umbrella evidence behind a structured neuromuscular warm-up once lacrosse resumes. Caveats: the evidence is mostly from female athletes, uninjured populations and injury-prevention outcomes, and it mixes randomised and non-randomised studies.
relevance.thorborg-2017-fifa-11plus: The best-studied field-sport warm-up and the template most lacrosse prevention warm-ups borrow from. Soccer is a field sport with similar cutting demands, but there is no lacrosse trial. The app's own warm-up (bike plus knee circuit) is not the 11+.
relevance.slauterbeck-2019-fifa-11plus-high-school: An honest counterweight to the positive meta-analyses: benefit depends on actually doing the warm-up regularly. It came up in a lacrosse search, but the abstract does not split out lacrosse results.
relevance.lauersen-2014-exercise-prevention: Supports keeping balance work and strength in the programme long term, and not relying on stretching as a warm-up. This is prevention in healthy athletes, not rehab.
relevance.su-2025-balance-acl-soccer: The most recent synthesis linking balance work inside warm-ups to fewer ACL injuries, with a male subgroup. Balance was bundled with other components, so its effect alone is not isolated, and some included studies were not randomised.
relevance.fitzgerald-2000-perturbation-nonoperativ: The closest population in this search: non-operative knee ligament rehab in athletes returning to cutting sports. The training was perturbation on moving surfaces, not static eyes-closed stance. It is a classic primary study.
relevance.arundale-2017-acl-sports-men: Suggests that once strength, agility and prevention work are in place, as in Phase 3, extra balance perturbation adds little. Population is male, which matches Shawn, but surgical.
relevance.arumugam-2021-nmt-proprioception: An honest limit on what balance work is shown to do for knee joint sense. Balance training is supported more for preventing injury than for restoring proprioception.
relevance.negahban-2014-single-leg-stance-untreate: The 'why this test' rationale for g1-stance: the eyes-closed condition is where side-to-side deficits showed after non-operative ligament injury, and both legs need training. It does not validate the 30 s cut-off.
relevance.yu-2025-postural-stability-update: A counterpoint to Negahban 2014: static stance is a coarse screen, so g1-stance is a floor check, not proof of readiness. Shows the evidence is mixed.
relevance.springer-2007-unipedal-stance-norms: Supports timing the stance as best of three and shows the test is reliable. The age-band norms are in the paywalled full text and were not read, so no number from it should appear in the app.
relevance.chmielewski-2016-plyo-intensity: Supports starting plyometrics at low intensity in Phase 3 without giving up the benefit. The trial was too small to show safety differences.
relevance.buckthorpe-2021-plyometric-recommendatio: Describes the same logic as Phase 3's ladder (two-foot pogos and stuck landings, then single-leg and repeated hops), and the app's clean-twice progression fits its criterion-based monitoring. It is opinion, not tested evidence.
relevance.kotsifaki-2023-aspetar-guideline: The most recent clinical practice guideline. Its 'Prognostic value of return to sport criteria' section (open-access full text) covers the hop-containing batteries. Its own discharge criteria use countermovement and drop-jump symmetry rather than single, triple or crossover distance hops, so it supports the gate as a consensus checklist, not a validated predictor, and does not endorse these exact hops.
relevance.alexander-2022-running-knee-injury: An honest note for the cardio pattern: the gradual 10-to-18-mile build is sensible but unproven as knee protection. The program's pain and next-morning monitoring does the real gating.
relevance.kerr-2017-ncaa-mens-lacrosse: Lacrosse-specific context for Phase 4: it explains why the ladder puts games last and keeps lower-limb prevention work going. The epidemiology is from men's lacrosse, but this is not a rehab or prevention trial.
relevance.ardern-2013-psychological-factors: The 'why this item' rationale for g3-trust (would you trust the knee at full speed): confidence and low fear go with a successful return. It shows association, not cause. Shared with the readiness researcher. The best broad rationale for the manual 'would trust it at full speed' item: confidence and fear affect return independently of physical tests. Not knee-specific.
relevance.xiao-2023-psych-readiness-acl: Supports checking readiness separately from physical tests (g3-trust next to g3-acl-rsi). It does not validate the 76 cut-off, and it is post-surgical. Shared with the readiness researcher.
relevance.liu-2026-hop-meta: Most recent synthesis on whether the gate's 90% hop line predicts anything. Caveat: the abstract also reports triple-hop symmetry of 90% or better slightly associated with HIGHER reinjury odds, a counterintuitive finding. The record is in PMC but not flagged open access; the full text was not read.
relevance.girdwood-2025-hop-trajectory: Supports testing hops in several directions and shows the three forward distance hops largely measure the same thing. The takeaway rests on the abstract; the full text was checked only for the certainty statement. It says nothing about the 6 m timed hop.
relevance.webster-2019-rts-battery-validity: Honest counterweight to treating a passed hop battery as clearance. Batteries in the included studies varied and were not limited to hops; a published reanalysis and critique exists (Capin et al. 2019, PMID 31289039, not added).
relevance.losciale-2020-hop-association: Explains why the hop items are a readiness check, not a reinjury predictor, and why KOOS and hops can disagree. The abstract does not list which hop tests were included.
relevance.grindem-2020-functional-readiness: Larger Delaware-Oslo follow-up supporting the 90% battery line. The confidence interval is wide, and the battery mixes strength, hops and questionnaires, so the hops' own share of the effect is not isolated.
relevance.noyes-1991-hop-tests: The classic origin of the four-hop battery the gate uses (the app's rule rests on it). Its population of non-reconstructed knees is closer to Shawn's than most. The abstract says four hop types without naming them. It supports reading a pass as weak evidence of normal function and a fail as a real flag.
relevance.reid-2007-hop-reliability: The measurement-properties source for the exact four-hop battery, including the 6 m timed hop (the app's g3-six-meter-timed-hop rests on this battery). Its minimal detectable change is a useful caution when a reading sits just under or just over the 90% line.
relevance.wood-2025-healthy-pass-rates: A limitation of symmetry thresholds: natural asymmetry exists. Gives context for a near miss on a hop item without changing the gate.
relevance.fitzgerald-2000-nonoperative-screening: One of the few hop-battery studies in a NON-OPERATIVE population, so it is closer to Shawn than the reconstruction literature. Here the hops screen early candidates rather than clear a late return. The abstract does not give thresholds.
relevance.webster-2008-acl-rsi-development: The development paper for the exact 12-item scale the app administers (the app's g3-acl-rsi rests on it). It proposes no cut-off, and validation is in reconstructed knees only.
relevance.webster-2018-acl-rsi-short: Shows the full and short versions behave similarly. This matters because the 76.7 cut-off was derived on the short version while the app scores the full 12-item scale. Similar is not identical, so carrying the cut-off across is an assumption.
relevance.mcpherson-2019-acl-rsi-second-injury: The published origin of the gate's 76 (76.7 points, 90% sensitivity). Caveats for the app: it was derived on the 6-item SHORT version, in patients aged 20 or under, 12 months after reconstruction, to screen for second ACL injury. Older patients showed no difference.
relevance.piussi-2022-pro-cutoffs: Direct counter-evidence to treating any single questionnaire cut-off (including 76) as a reinjury screen, from an older and larger cohort than McPherson's. Supports keeping KOOS informational (Progress only).
relevance.sadeqi-2018-acl-rsi-fast: Shows that published ACL-RSI thresholds depend on the outcome and the cohort. For return to the same sport, the best line here was lower than the gate's 76, which is the stricter figure derived from second-injury screening.
relevance.sell-2024-acl-rsi-over-time: Shows how hard a 76 line is to reach: pooled averages after reconstruction stay below it even at 2-5 years (about 71). The abstract stratifies only by early, delayed or unclear surgical approach and reports no non-operative pooling.
relevance.webster-2019-return-to-performance: Supports keeping a psychological readiness item (ACL-RSI) and the separate 'trust it' item alongside hop symmetry (single and triple crossover hops in this study). The outcome is return to performance, not reinjury.
relevance.hamrin-senorski-2025-rehab-alone-symmetr: A rare non-operative comparison. It suggests a non-surgical knee can test symmetric while confidence lags, which is why the trust item stays separate from the symmetry items. Symmetry here is isokinetic strength, not hops.
relevance.cuyul-vasquez-2022-cross-education-acl: Supports that the good leg's single-leg work is not wasted for the injured side. Post-surgical population with early restricted loading; the program trains both legs, injured side first, so this is a supporting idea, not a reason to train the good leg alone.
relevance.valdes-2026-cross-education-clinical: Most recent synthesis; tempers the ACL-specific review by finding no significant effect in musculoskeletal patients or for the lower limb. Show both.
relevance.spiering-2021-minimal-dose: Supports keeping loads unchanged while cutting sets on deload weeks, and keeping upper-body intensity up while the knee limits other work. The authors say data for athletes are insufficient.
relevance.acsm-2009-progression-models: General backing for the pressing and pulling slots and their double progression. Healthy adults; nothing specific to training around a knee injury. Pre-dates GRADE-style grading.
relevance.zazulak-2007-trunk-control-knee: Classic study behind 'the core protects the knee'. Prediction in healthy athletes, mostly female-driven; it does not show core training changes the outcome for a male lacrosse player.
relevance.ellestad-2024-loaded-carry: The only carry-specific study found that fits: shows the farmer's carry is trunk work. Muscle activation only; no strength, injury or rehab outcome.
relevance.mccrary-2015-upper-body-warm-up: Supports lighter sets of the same lift before the working sets on pressing slots. Its own finding: no injury-prevention evidence exists.
relevance.ribeiro-2014-warm-up-resistance: Honest counterweight: warm-up sets are not shown to add reps. The app's ramp is display-only and costs only time, so this does not argue against it, but it should not be sold as a performance boost.
relevance.wilson-2025-muscle-warm-up-force: Most recent synthesis on warm-up and muscle function. Mechanism-level only; nothing on ramp sets before lifting or on knee safety.
